data.title: Laird Superfood Appoints Mark Johnson as Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
Laird Superfood Appoints Mark Johnson as Chief Financial Officer

Seasoned CPG finance executive brings more than 25 years of experience across beverage, food, and premium pet food.

Laird Superfood, Inc. (NYSE American: LSF) today announced the appointment of Mark Johnson as Chief Financial Officer, effective October 1, 2026. Mr. Johnson will report to Chief Executive Officer Jason Vieth and will serve as the Company’s principal financial officer and principal accounting officer.

Mr. Johnson brings more than 25 years of finance leadership across public consumer packaged goods and private equity-backed companies. He joins Laird Superfood from Tropicana Brands Group, where he served as Vice President of Finance – North America. Previously, he was Vice President – Commercial & Supply Chain Finance at Champion Petfoods, and held multiple finance leadership roles at Danone / WhiteWave Foods and The Pepsi Bottling Group. Mr. Johnson holds an M.B.A. with a concentration in finance from the Carlson School of Management at the University of Minnesota and a Bachelor of Arts in Economics from the University of Wisconsin Madison.

“Mark brings the kind of operating finance experience this next chapter calls for - scaling brands in food and beverage inside businesses held to a high bar on discipline and returns,” said Jason Vieth, Chief Executive Officer of Laird Superfood. “As we integrate our recent acquisitions and build toward sustainable, profitable growth, his experience will be a real asset to our team.”

“Laird Superfood has built genuine brand equity in better-for-you food and beverage, and the platform the team has assembled has meaningful room to grow,” said Mr. Johnson. “I’m excited to join at this point in the Company’s development and to help translate that momentum into durable financial performance.”

About Laird Superfood

Laird Superfood, Inc. creates award-winning, plant-based superfood products that are clean, delicious, and functional. Our products are designed to enhance a consumer's daily ritual and keep them fueled naturally throughout the day. Laird Superfood was co-founded in 2015 by the world's most prolific big-wave surfer, Laird Hamilton. Laird Superfood's offerings are environmentally conscientious, responsibly tested and made with real ingredients. Shop all products online at www.lairdsuperfood.com and join the Laird Superfood community on social media for the latest news and daily doses of inspiration.

data.title: High School Students Save on College and Launch Rewarding Careers While Earning Their Diploma
data.description:
High School Students Save on College and Launch Rewarding Careers While Earning Their Diploma

Learn4Life’s dual enrollment programs offer a plethora of opportunities

Dual enrollment courses help high schoolers at Learn4Life earn college credits and prepare for rewarding careers

With college tuition and student loan debt continuing to rise1, families are looking for help. September is College Savings Month to remind us about the importance of saving for college, and various tax breaks and options to start a college fund.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260904902450/en/

Dual enrollment courses help high schoolers at Learn4Life earn college credits and prepare for rewarding careers

Another way to save on the cost of college is for students to take dual enrollment courses while they are still in high school. They can earn college credits while they work toward a high school diploma.

Learn4Life, a network of 90+ public high schools, offers dual enrollment programs in a range of industries, from healthcare, trades and culinary to business and information technology.

Learn4Life alumni Summer H. was fascinated by the cognitive development of children – something she had been exploring in college dual enrollment classes while working toward graduation at Learn4Life High Schools.

“We learned about the milestones in cognition for different age groups and how they tie to behavior patterns,” she said. “I want a career where I can contribute to children’s lives by providing the best environment for learning.”

Summer earned a Child Development Professional (CDP) Assistant Permit from West Hills Community College and landed a job at a childcare center.

The career opportunities are wide open, from working as a nanny or in a daycare center, to pursuing degrees in teaching or even child psychology.

“Our schools offer personalized instruction that is tailored to each student. We work with them to find a career path that fits their skills and interests,” said Shellie Hanes, Learn4Life superintendent of schools. “Many teens are not even thinking about college until we show them the possibilities. With dual enrollment, they can explore various careers in the safe environment of our high schools.”

Hanes points out that students who are enrolled in dual enrollment programs are more excited about coming to school and do better in all their subjects than students who don’t.

“Plus, they are learning how to self-motivate and complete the coursework in a timely manner,” Hanes said. “It’s wonderful to see how students find something they like and pursue it with a passion.”

For more information, visit www.Learn4Life.org.

About Learn4Life

Learn4Life is a network of nonprofit public high schools that provide students personalized learning, career training and life skills. Each school is locally controlled, tuition free and gives students the flexibility and one-on-one attention they need to succeed. Serving more than 64,000 students through a year-round program, we help them prepare for a future beyond high school. For more information, please visit www.learn4life.org.

1 https://educationdata.org/cost-of-a-college-class-or-credit-hour#:~:text=The%20average%20public%2C%204%2Dyear,hour%20or%20%24426%20per%20course

data.title: Novartis Says Pelacarsen Heart Disease Drug Missed Primary Endpoint — Update
data.description:
By Elias Schisgall 




  Novartis said a heart disease drug did not meet its primary endpoint in a Phase 3 study. 



  The company on Friday said that the drug, pelacarsen, did not reduce the risk of cardiovascular events--including deaths, heart attacks, and strokes--compared to a placebo. 



  The drug did succeed in lowering lipoprotein(a) levels, Novartis said. 



  "These are not the results we hoped for, but they provide important evidence that advances scientific understanding of the relationship between Lp(a) lowering and cardiovascular outcomes and may help inform future approaches to cardiovascular risk management," Chief Medical Officer Shreeram Aradhye said. 



  Pelacarsen was initially discovered and developed by Ionis Pharmaceuticals, before Novartis exercised an option to license development and commercialization rights for the drug in 2019. 



  Shares of Novartis declined 4.4% to $153.00 in after-hours trading on Friday. Ionis shares were flat.

data.title: Tata Motors Launches Bid for Iveco Group
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis 




  Italian vehicle maker Iveco Group said Tata Motors has launched an all-cash voluntary offer for the company, offering EUR14.10 in cash per share. 



  The offer values Iveco Group at about EUR3.82 billion, the companies said. 



  The tender offer is being made via TML CV Holdings, a Dutch subsidiary of Tata Motors. 



   Iveco said its board unanimously supports the offer, and recommends shareholders accept the deal. Under the terms of the deal, Tata will acquire 100% of the Iveco's common shares and delist the company from Euronext Milan. 



  Iveco said Exor, its largest shareholder, has irrevocably committed to support the offer. 



  The companies also said they believe having Iveco operate as a wholly privately owned subsidiary is key to the sustainable success of its business and long-term value creation. Tata will respect existing rights and benefits of Iveco's employees, and doesn't envisage any reduction of the workforce of Iveco Group as a direct consequence of the combination, the companies added. 



  Iveco's brands include FPT, Iveco Bus, and finance arm Iveco Capital. 



  Shareholders will vote on the transaction at a meeting scheduled for Oct. 16.
